description: ONE row, full 3-stage chain. A brief with a stated audience, a stated ask, and enough named figures that every stage has something real to be judged on: a plan that omits a required subject is visible, a deck that invents its numbers is visible, and a validator that changes nothing is visible.

rows.prompt: Build a Series B pitch deck for Cadence, a workforce-scheduling SaaS selling to mid-market healthcare systems. Audience: growth-stage investors, 20 minutes, deck read cold before the meeting. The ask is $28M at a $140M pre-money to fund a US clinical-staffing expansion. Cover, in this order: the problem (nurse scheduling churn), the product, traction, unit economics, market, competition, the roadmap, the team, and the ask. Traction to show: ARR $4.2M growing 118% year over year, 61 hospital customers, net revenue retention 134%, gross margin 79%, CAC payback 14 months, logo churn 4%. Include a bar chart of quarterly ARR across the last eight quarters ending at $4.2M, and a cohort chart showing net revenue retention by signing year for 2022, 2023 and 2024. Competition should be a positioning table against three named incumbents on scheduling automation, clinical compliance, and integration depth. Team slide covers four founders with real-sounding healthcare-operations backgrounds. Keep it factual and quantitative — no marketing adjectives without a number behind them.
